That's too bad if that's the case. I understand wanting to appeal to a wider audience, but it's sad when games lose what they are at their core in the process. Call of Duty is actually a good example of this.

Modern Warfare and Black Ops both used to have a slower playing style. It was still run and gun, but at least you were penalized for running around blindly. Your sight-up speed is slower than someone who is stationary or walking, and there were ways to ambush people who weren't paying attention. Then Ghosts flopped, people complained, the series was blindsided by Titanfall, and Sledgehammer took the franchise to the extreme with Advanced Warfare, catering to the twitch-style gameplay and removing most of the penalties for running around blindly. What does sight-up speed matter when you can instantly jet-pack into the air and start raining bullets?

Some series can adapt and innovate without losing their core focus, but unfortunately it seems like the longer a series goes the more likely it is to lose what it is at its core. Resident Evil is another one that used to be all about suspense and horror, but is more about super-powered beings and over the top villains. I'm impressed that Metal Gear has held onto its stealth roots so well and has managed to adapt an open-world gameplay with MGSV without drifting from its focus. I think it just depends on the series and what the priority is. Oftentimes appealing to a wider audience means losing out on core fans who supported it from the beginning.

It's not the case with FO4 though, at least in my opinion.

Yes, they streamlined tons of things but not necessarily in a bad way. Skills are gone and essentially replaced by the perks system. For example, this means that you can specialize into some specific types of weapons to use them to their full potential if you level up the respective perks, but you don't get effectively locked out of using certain weapons just because you didn't invest arbitrary skill points into their respective skills. I thought it was always stupid that you could have 100% in Small Guns skill and be incredibly adept at popping heads with pistols from miles away, yet when you picked up an energy pistol, you couldn't hit the broad side of a barn because it was arbitrarily linked to an entirely different skill. Now you can pick up both guns and have the same base line of effectiveness with them, and if you've invested in the Gunslinger perk you'll actually be just as adept with an energy pistol as with a normal pistol, but unless you take the perk for semi automatic rifles you'll be just as (in)effective with a hunting rifle as you are with a laser rifle. Similar stuff applies to automatic rifles, melee weapons, etc. This is a much better system in my opinion.

They have also increased complexity in a lot of areas. The crafting system is great and, also allows specializing into niches, and it's the most complex it's ever been in any Fallout game. Combat arguably as well.

Looting and inventory management has also been streamlined (thank god the game doesn't pop up a menu that pauses the entire game for every single container I open anymore).

I don't mind the simplified dialogue system and voiced protagonist myself, it gets the job done, but I suppose I can see why people might have their beef with it, but then, again, it gets the job done and the game is built around it, it's just a different approach than the previous system.

At the end of the day, it's of course all a subjective. I've played FO1, 2 and Tactics back in the day when they were released, they're some of the best games I've ever played, especially for their era, but those game mechanics haven't aged well (again, my subjective opinion) and I probably couldn't stand to play through a game with FO1's combat system anymore in this day and age, and I think the evolution the franchise has taken turned out great. I've had at least as much fun with FO3 and NV than I did with 1 and 2 and I remember many, many people complaining massively about how shitty FO3 was because it wasn't true to the original and yadda yadda. Heck, I remember people saying the exact thing about FO2 over FO1. And now it's the same with FO4.

I've had great funin the ~10hrs or so I got to spend on it so far, and the impression seems to be shared by everyone on my friends list playing it right now, a lot of people are enjoying FO4 and I think it's a bit bewildering to call this phenomenon "disappointing".

I can sympathize if people just say "FO4 is not my kind of game, I just can't enjoy it because of [X]", that's a subjective and fair statement, but the general trend, especially here on Voat, of lashing out against the game and Bethesda because any change to any aspect of the game compared to previous iterations has to be per se awful mixed with the load of bullshit people throw around ("VATS has been removed", seriously?) and getting downvoated just because you dare say that you find something positive about the game is getting absurd.
